title: Bloemgracht 82, the resistance attic raided ten days before liberation
check_note: The register records a 1945 stone with the names Dick Wolters and Ko Stevesen; the 2014 stone gives the right names. Is the old stone still there beside it?

title: Cineac, Duiker's newsreel cinema
check_note: Last confirmed use is a club (2007); check who uses the building now and whether the corner canopy and booth window are still as described.

title: De Vorstenlanden, Eduard Huf's cigar shop in the Zoutsteeg
check_note: The register (2006) says the shop name is under white paint, Amsterdam op de kaart (2017) reads it on the frieze; check how legible it is, and the café's name (Kadinsky in 2014).

title: Gerzon's fashion works, where a thousand seamstresses sewed
check_note: Current hotel taken from an undated page (joodsamsterdam.nl, an NH hotel); check the operator and name on site.

title: Huis met de Neuzen (the House with the Noses)
check_note: The register says three caricature heads; whether all three are still in place and where exactly on the front was not checked.

title: Kettner's piano shop, with its wares in tiles
check_note: Check which shop uses the building now and whether the firm's name still stands in the railing on the roof ridge.

title: Maison Stroucken, the party hall inside DeLaMar
check_note: Gebouwd in Amsterdam says the front is partly a replica; no source (searched 24 Nov 2026) says whether the winged dog and the stair turrets were rebuilt. Needs a look on site.

title: Odeon, from brewery to concert hall to gay disco
check_note: Tenants confirmed to 2017-2018 (Supperclub, cocktail bar); check who is in the building in 2026 and whether the lamb is still on the gable.

title: Reestraat 6, where Anton de Kom lived
check_note: No plaque for De Kom is known; check whether one is on the front.

title: Schiller, the painter-hotelier's hotel
check_note: Café Schiller (no. 24A) has a live site with opening hours (Nov 2026); NH Schiller hotel not confirmed for 2026 (nh-hotels.com refused the request).

title: The meat hall on the old Westerkerk graveyard
check_note: The register says it has been a restaurant since about 2000; the current business was not confirmed.

title: Two schools on the old Leidse cemetery
check_note: The TV company left Raamplein 1 around 2018; what the building is used for now is not known.

title: Walenweeshuis, the Walloon orphanage waiting for a future
check_note: Check whether restoration works have started (scaffolding, fences, permit notice) and whether any part is open to the public

title: Beta berlayar jauh, the Moluccan marines' monument
check_note: Sources place it on the Voorwerf; the pin is an estimate, no exact spot or photo found.

title: De Swarte Mvele and the De Vries van Buuren building (Waterlooplein 3)
check_note: Pin is near the corner of Waterlooplein 3; set it on the stone in the Zwanenburgwal side wall

title: Leidse Dwarstuin, a walled garden in the tourist strip
check_note: Pin at the address of the garden gate (Lange Leidsedwarsstraat 152); exact entrance to confirm.

title: Mbulu Ngulu, an African guardian of the dead on an advertising column
check_note: Moved in 2019 to the Sarphatistraat end across the Oostenburgergracht; pin on the new spot, confirm the exact column.

title: Noordermarkt: the post, the plaque and the outline in the paving
check_note: The pin is on the Woutertje Pieterse statue; the water-tap post stands near it.

title: Roeterseiland: the building with its legs cut off, and the lawn that was saved and lost
check_note: The pin is on the canal under the bridge building (REC B/C); the exact span of the building over the water was not checked on site.

title: The Knobbeliep, Amsterdam's own knobbly elm
check_note: Pin from the city tree register (tree 341941); confirm which Westermarkt elm it is on site.

title: The floating gardens of Robert Jasper Grootveld, Wittenburgervaart
check_note: The rafts lie near the Ezelsbrug, diagonally opposite the Bandenboot; pin approximate on the water.

title: The rooster of De Haan's matzo factory (Valkenburgerstraat)
check_note: Sources differ on where inside the stone hangs (the hall of the flats or the parking garage entrance) and whether it can be seen from outside

title: Tuin Bickersgracht Noordkop and children's farm De Dierencapel
check_note: Pin on the farm entrance; the exact edge of the neighbours' garden beside the skate ramp to be confirmed on site.

title: Waterline, a red figure on the quay wall
check_note: Pin approximate; place the figure exactly and confirm it is still there.

title: Catharinahofje, Egelantiersgracht (former)
check_note: Is the Vierhuizengang under the stoops of nos. 203-213 still open? One source says it vanished with the new building, the city's alley map still lists it.

title: De Nederlander, a biscuit factory with three step gables
check_note: Amsterdam op de kaart (last checked by its editors some years ago) names an antiques dealer on the ground floor; not confirmed recently.

title: Elizabeth Wolffschool, a public school for paying girls
check_note: The register (about 2005) says it is still a school, run privately; check what uses the building now.

title: Lifeboat shed on the Windroosplein
check_note: Reopened Oct 2026 as event venue Amsterdam Wharf after a full rebuild (amsterdamwharf.nl, Nov 2026). Is the society's painted name still on both walls?

title: Olieslagerssteeg, the lepers' house, the oil pressers and Maison de Bonneterie
check_note: The staff plaque was inside the store, closed since 2014; whether it is still there is not known.

title: Sint Luciënsteeg, the gable stone wall
check_note: Rebuilding of the museum began September 2026; check whether the wall is screened by the works, and fix the pin on the stones.

title: The Russensjoel and the old "Jodenkerkstraat" (Nieuwe Kerkstraat 149)
check_note: Whether the Russian sjoel still holds services; the latest known listing (2004) gives Shabbat and festival mornings.

title: The harmonica player of the Anjeliersstraat, by a sculptor nobody names
check_note: The latest dated mention of the harmonica player is from 2017; confirm it and which small figures still hang in the street.

title: The phone box library of the Boomstraat
check_note: Latest dated report is November 2021; confirm the box and its spot (pinned at no. 67).

title: Trompettersteeg, the narrowest alley and its hidden coat of arms
check_note: No evidence of the coat of arms or the sailors after 2021; check both on site.

title: Walraven van Hall's snapped tree and the Navalny memorial, Frederiksplein
check_note: Latest evidence of Van der Linden's painted acacia on the square is from 2018, before the bank's rebuild of 2020-2025.
